new_statements.citation: Reed, Wes (data checked by; SIL PNG Branch). 2000. Organised Phonology Data: Yopno Language [YUT], Morobe Province. 4 pp. Manuscript, SIL Ukarumpa (PDF printed 21 Sep 2004). SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 42339.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (4 pp., native text layer, PDF metadata: Title "OPD", Author "SIL PNG Branch", created 2004-09-20). Page 3 (header "Yupna (Yopno) OPD Printed: September 21, 2004 Page 3") contains, verbatim, the heading "Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)" followed by the single line "Stress is contrastive occurring on first or second syllable." Nothing else on stress, tone or length in that section; the only other prosodic remark is under Conventions: Phonological, "/ɨ/ is inherently longer than other vowels." No stressed forms or minimal pairs anywhere in the OPD (the consonant/vowel example lists and the syllable-pattern list are unmarked for stress). The heading is the OPD template heading, s…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is lexically contrastive; it falls on either the first or the second syllable of the word, and which one is not predictable from the source's statement (no rule, no minimal pairs and no stressed examples are given). Note that Claassen & McElhanon 1970: 66 judged stress 'probably sub-phonemic in Yupna' with a light functional load, so the contrastiveness claim is not uncontested.
new_statements.exceptions: None mentioned; the one-line statement gives no examples. The OPD notes /ɨ/ is inherently longer than other vowels and says nothing about tone. Claassen & McElhanon 1970: 66 (survey) say 'Stress is phonemic in Rawa but probably sub-phonemic in Yupna and Wantoat. In none of these languages does it carry a heavy functional load.'
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (the OPD's phonemic-inventory format lists stress under word suprasegmentals); no phrase-level statement. Data is the SIL Keweng/Tepmangi-area variety (major villages listed: Keweng, Tepmangi, Nokopo, Gua, Isan, Wandabo); the OPD header calls the language 'Yupna (Yopno)'.
new_statements.identity_note: Reed 2000 OPD describes 'Yopno Language [YUT]', header 'Yupna (Yopno)', Morobe Province, villages Keweng, Tepmangi, Nokopo, Gua, Isan, Wandabo -- i.e. the SIL working variety of Yopno = yopn1238 (dialects Kewieng, Nokopo, Wandabong, Isan per Wikipedia). Claassen & McElhanon 1970 use 'Yupna' for the same language. Slotta's materials are on the Nian/Nokopo dialect.
